extracted.intended_audience: mothers, housewives, and family heads (middle-class American households)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and standards for household conduct, family music, religious upbringing, temperance, treatment of boys, and practical cookery aimed at mothers and household managers. The text gives behavioral norms, educational recommendations, and practical tips for running a moral and well-ordered home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promoting or providing intoxicating liquors
rubrics_metrics.description: Practically: 'Woe unto him that putteth the cup to his neighbor's lips!' — do not lend the weight of a straw to another's downward slide by offering or facilitating alcohol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotal justification: scenes of convivial drinking led to ruined lives (one brother died of delirium tremens; others ruined). The author states: 'Had I my way, not one drop of intoxicating liquors should be sold, except by druggists, and then only by a physician's prescription.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve alcohol for judicious medicinal use, not habitual beverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Alcohol (brandy, wine, whiskey) has inestimable value as medicine when used judiciously, but is nearly worthless and harmful when the system is accustomed to it as a daily or frequent beverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author acknowledges that 'judicious use of them as restoratives has saved many lives' but warns against everyday consumption; distinguishes therapeutic uses from habitual drinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasional culinary use of alcohol is permissible unless it tempts a drinker
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no sin or danger in the occasional use of spirits in cooking (e.g., a tablespoon in pudding-sauce or a wineglass in jelly) unless a family member already 'loves and craves the stimulant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule: the housemother knows her guests; omit alcoholic flavoring if any family member is susceptible. The same person tempted by table wine may be tempted by communion wine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual conscience and communal responsibility regarding temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each person bears responsibility of principle and action; one should not be troubled if others think one's creed goes too far or too short, but one should 'lift my hand in protest' against toleration of what leads to inebriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral stance: be outspoken in protesting 'the crying sin of the age' while respecting individual conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach and maintain household vocal music (singing by note and part-songs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Households should preserve the practice of singing by note and part-songs taught in church or singing-school so that 'every household possessed and made frequent use' of vocal collections and could sing simple church tunes at sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to historical resources (Boston Academy, Carmina Sacra, the Shawm). Argues that family music fostered widespread musical ability and enjoyment and should be revived rather than surrendered to professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid professionalizing home music and silencing amateurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist the trend where a single professionally-minded musician in a household becomes hypercritical, driving amateurs away and turning home music into a spectacle for professionals only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a 'music-mad family' or a trained singer who refuses to sing except when 'in perfect tune' discourage communal singing; the author urges the true artist to encourage tyros rather than disdain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate musical education of the many to create genuine appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical education should be broad and popular (like the German model) so the general public can intelligently enjoy and discriminate in music rather than deferring entirely to professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: German artisan's ear and voice are cultivated from childhood—resulting in hearty, intelligent enjoyment; reviving singing-schools and ballad traditions would improve domestic and public music-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve simple domestic music traditions (ballads, part-songs, family evenings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple family music—ballads, sea songs, love songs with choruses, Sunday-evening group singing—enrich homes and should be retained even as musical tastes evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists examples ('Nelly Was a Lady', 'Old Kentucky Home') and emphasizes clear enunciation of words and communal participation across generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents should actively instruct children in Scripture and family religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Children of today are often less familiar with Holy Scripture, Bible history, and cardinal Protestant doctrines than children of fifty years ago; parents (especially mothers) must take responsibility for religious instruction and family devotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical practices: family Bible reading, studying Sunday-school lessons at home, memorizing Psalms and New Testament passages, catechism questions, and regular family prayers and hymns. The author testifies from long experience as a Bible-class teacher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not outsource children's religious formation entirely to Sunday-school
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'contract system' in religious teaching—where students or parents expect the Sunday-school teacher to do all preparation—is inadequate; the home must not abdicate its instructional role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique: many parents let children 'press the button' (attend only), leaving teachers to do the rest; results in superficial religious knowledge and weaker attachment to church worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mother as first religious teacher and moral exemplar in the home
rubrics_metrics.description: The mother is described as 'the baby's first altar' and 'priestess' who must gather children for confession, counsel, and prayer, cultivating sanctity and love for the church and its worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mothers faithfully train children with sacred songs, Bible stories, and tender talk of the Saviour's love, children will grow to find the church 'amiable' and worthy of fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide boys a respectable, individualized 'den' (living space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boys should be given decent, pride-inspiring lodging comparable to daughters' rooms; neglecting or packing them into shabby back-rooms breeds humiliation and may push them away from home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: contrast between well-appointed sisters' rooms and a brother's dingy back-room; recommendation to remove 'incurables' (worn furniture) and furnish a boy's room to express maternal love and desire for his welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance respecting a boy's individuality with maintaining cleanliness and order
rubrics_metrics.description: While boys are naturally less tidy, mothers should ensure rooms are 'clean and bright' without rigid surveillance; avoid meddling with personal papers while preventing squalor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical counsel: clean glaring disorders but allow personal imprint and avoid over-management that would 'irk him'; 'the boy is worth more than the room.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Value tasteful, economical cookery—favor flavor and daintiness, not only fillingness
rubrics_metrics.description: American cookery tends toward 'fillingness' and quick recipes, but would benefit from French-style attention to daintiness and flavor without sacrificing economy of time and fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: show that economical alternatives (e.g., stock from cracked bones + vegetables) produce nourishing dinners; quick desserts like blanc-mange or junket can be inexpensive and tasteful; practical demonstrations may persuade housewives who prioritize speed and quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on salted meats, excessive fats, and cheap substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The staple American household diet often overuses salt pork, salt beef, salt fish, and frying fats to 'fill' appetites, while neglecting eggs, poultry, fresh vegetables and fruits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nutrition guidance: use cabbage and potatoes to prevent scurvy, but seek variety; encourage use of eggs and poultry more often; criticizes extreme thrift that barters butter and fresh produce away for groceries and cheap cooking butter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use economical kitchen practices (use scraps to make stock, reuse resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy in the kitchen can be both time- and fuel-saving and nutritionally beneficial: e.g., simmer cracked bones, carrot, onion, and herbs to make soup stock on a side of the range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable practical tip: set stock to simmer on washing-day to yield base for multiple dinners; such practices 'waste neither time nor fuel' and yield better meals than rapid, wasteful shortcuts.
